# The premise ledger

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [中文](../../../../README.zh.md) · **Read** · [One page](../../ONE-PAGE.md) · [The theory](../../THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md) · [Chapters](../../chapters/README.md) · [Uses](../../USES.md) · **Check** · [Tests](../../../../TESTS.md) · [Results](../../../../RESULTS.md) · [Proofs](../../../../MAP.md#check-the-proofs-yourself) · [Open questions](../../../../OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) · [Reviewers](../../review/README.md) · **See** · [Atlas](ATLAS.md) · [Graph](../THEORY-GRAPH.md) · [Connections](CROSSWALK.md) · [How it grew](../../../LINEAGE.md) · [Glossary](../../../../GLOSSARY.md) · [Where everything is](../../../../MAP.md)

The atlas's views: [the atlas](ATLAS.md) · **the premise ledger** · [the terrain](TERRAIN.md) · [tests bound](BINDINGS.md) · [situations](SITUATIONS.md) · [the crosswalk](CROSSWALK.md) · [what does not join](JOINS.md)

*AI-written, from the entries (PLAN §13, step 2). A premise here is a hypothesis a law takes, a commitment the representation makes, or a premise of dynamics, correspondence, ethics or practice that 08 §4 lists, with the Lean that states it, where it is shown holding and failing, the dynamics whose laws take it and the exits that leave by dropping it. Every list is read off the entries at each render; none is typed. A premise is no result and the ledger proves nothing; whether one holds of an actual system is never established here.*

How the lists are read. **For every family read, a law's list names every hypothesis its Lean statement binds:** each binder whose type is a proposition, explicit, implicit or an instance, before the colon or a leading hypothesis after it, mapped to the premise it states. For families C and D, on 10 November 2026, a script read them off the elaborated statements of the 344 laws in the Becoming core, the extractors read them off the source for the 40 in the periphery, and a checker set to refute read every mapping ([their mapping](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/development/aa-attractor-atlas/step2b/mapping.json)). For families A, B, E, F, G and H, on 11 November, a script read them off the elaborated statements of 1,504 laws in the core, the extractors read them off the source for the 151 in the periphery, and a checker per share, set to refute, read in full every mapping to a premise new to the ledger and every one that departed from a script's guess, and sampled the rest ([their mapping](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/development/aa-attractor-atlas/six/mapping.json)). A list also names premises a law takes another way, as the extractors, checkers and readers found them: definitions its statement is made through (the pool of readers, the rule after shaping, selection on listed counts; not every such definition is listed), commitments of the representation (natural-number amounts, requirements as thresholds, pointwise statements), premises a law holds by its form (Unread where nothing beyond the share is read; Accrues where the course's loss grows by one a step by its definition; the in-sync start where the course starts at the rule read from its counts), and premises taken through data, not through a proposition: decided, through binders of type Decidable, DecidableEq, DecidablePred or DecidableRel, instances or explicit (read off the elaborated statements for the six families' core laws; a binder stating P ∨ ¬ P maps to decided as a proposition); a supplied law of exchange; and others present in every count of carriers and others, a field of `CarrierCounts`, on the 54 laws whose statements are on such counts (found by a script reading the statements' constants, 51, and those of the definitions they name, 3 more on groups through `RuleShaping.Grouped`). So “none listed” says the statement binds no hypothesis and none of the others was found; still read the law's statement before applying it. One proposition (the same definition, its parameters in the same roles) is one premise, whether or not a law passes it to another, with one pair kept as two because existing premises keep their ids: a positive mass under the first hypothesis's weight, under a likelihood (`lumpedseeking-weighs`) and under the seeking weight (`expectedfreeenergyreals-weighs`); one name with two senses (ReadsShare on the rule and on the reading) is two. A census of what stands (`Web.StandingCensus`), embodiment of what arises (`World.ArisingEmbodied`), and enclosure around a family (`Flow.Around`) or around what stands (`Flow.AroundStanding`) are premises of their own: K3's coverage counts them under its census, embodiment and enclosure, but each states another proposition in the Lean. Where two shares named one proposition twice, or one law's binder twice, one id is kept (the pass's integrate-report.txt lists the merges, and its integrate.py and the checkers' files say why). The ledger is not uniform in two respects: one proposition stated at one step and at every step of a stretch is one premise in some places (as `runaway-supported` already was) and two in others, and a bound with the same symbols in two modules is one premise in some places and two in others. Discrete steps is taken by every law read that runs on steps (a course, a run or an orbit) and is listed on none; laws with no step index (for example `Diagonal.gap_unsaid` and `claims_incomplete`, the fixed-point laws of reflexive prediction, the free-energy minimizer, and laws on the rule read at one share such as `DrawnShaping.critical_iff`) do not take it. Natural-number amounts is listed on every law taking Accrues (at least one a step) and where a reader found a statement turning on the least unit. An exit drops the premise its law shows failing as the course leaves; where its law reads beyond the share, it drops Unread. Where an exit drops several, its law may show only that not all of them hold, not which fails (`Web.consumed_continues_transformed`, `rise_from_rest_or_open`). The joined laws of the lock it leaves hold Unread by their form, the loss there unread, and list it (`ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss`, `lock_line`), as `ChoiceCountCapture.counted_outlives_loss` does, whose lock no exit leaves this way; elsewhere the laws of the lock left hold it by having nothing beyond the share, and do not list it (`ClosedCapture.Drawn.through_locks`, `DrawnShaping.drawn_locks`, `RuleCapture.locked_stays`).

1693 premises. The laws and exits read for them so far: family A (30 dynamics), family B (26 dynamics), family C (17 dynamics), family D (22 dynamics), family E (10 dynamics), family F (24 dynamics), family G (18 dynamics), family H (37 dynamics). A premise whose statement is withheld is one whose home is being re-said; its statement waits for that.
